summary: AR-2: V19 adds governed policy tables, per-CSI counters, `pruned_at` and a SQL prune function. It replaces two V14/V15 guard functions with CREATE OR REPLACE. Each replacement permits exactly one new transition, and every other column and table keeps its old behaviour. The execution error vocabulary (ExecutionErrorCode, openapi ExecutionErrorCode, V13 CHECK) is NOT touched. ErrorCodeVocabularyTest therefore stays as it is. New guided codes are POLICY_NOT_APPROVED (v3 error enum), the clarification reason SIDE_EFFECT_CONFIRMATION and the prompt CONFIRM_ACTION, and the internal audit reasons UNGROUNDED_TARGET, DESTRUCTIVE_VERB and SIDE_EFFECT_DENIED under the existing POLICY_DENIED. AR-3: the missing key is `400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED`, thrown as StudioValidationException from StudioController.executeTest. Neither IdempotencyFilter nor ChecksExceptionHandler is edited for it. The P1 deletion is narrower than the plan assumed: claimAt/refusal/admit are live code under claimObserved and stay. Eight further test files call AdmissionCasService.claim() directly and are re-pointed by name.
verifiedFactsBearingOnTheRulings: The three-way 'one vocabulary' is the EXECUTION error vocabulary: dto/ExecutionErrorCode (10 values), openapi components.schemas.ExecutionErrorCode, and the V13 CHECK ck_ui_test_executions_error_code (V13:427-431). ErrorCodeVocabularyTest reads all three and also asserts that NO migration other than V13 names that constraint. A V19 that widened it would turn that test red by design.

Guided codes live in a different vocabulary set: v3 error.schema.json `code` (closed enum of 27 values that includes BUDGET_EXCEEDED, without POLICY_DENIED or CONFIGURATION_DENIED); v3 result.schema.json `errorCode` (an OPEN string 1..256 that excludes only AUTH_CONNECTION_REQUIRED); v3 ledger.schema.json outcomeCode (contains POLICY_DENIED); v3 clarification.schema.json `reason`/`promptCode` (closed). No DB CHECK constrains guided error codes. progress.errorCode is unconstrained jsonb.

GuidedSessionException.response() is the guided refusal envelope {schemaVersion 3, code, messageCode, requestId, retryable:false}. GuidedSessionController:103 maps it. No route in this backend emits application/problem+json. Studio handlers use ErrorResponse {error, message}. Filters use PlatformErrorResponse {error:{code,message}}.
startGuidedSession (openapi :1172) declares no 429, although GuidedSessionService.start already throws BUDGET_EXCEEDED 429 (maxSourceSteps, :530).

GuidedTranslationService.stopRejected (:1170) maps validator POLICY_DENIED/EVIDENCE_MISMATCH/REFERENCE_MISMATCH to terminal INVALID_CONTRACT. POLICY_DENIED is not repaired (repairs are only INVALID_CONTRACT and BINDING_ORDER, :1136). POLICY_DENIED is in the LOGIN_REQUIRED annotation set (:1124-1133).

V14 attempt guard (:351-360) refuses any change to an attempt whose status is not RESERVED/CALLING. GuidedTranslationStore.finishAttempt writes updated_at=clock_timestamp() on settlement only. GuidedPublicationEvidenceRepository.choiceWitness (:224) reads APPLIED safe_result NOT NULL only while publishing.

result() (GuidedSessionService:2272-2320) and GuidedPublicationResultProjector (:100-140) read only progress.stepIndex, errorCode and detail. publicationCommitted reads publicationRevisionId. Teardown writes teardownStatus after terminal (:2183). recordEvidence writes evidenceRef. annotateLoginFailure reads progress.observation, but only when NOT terminal (:273). read('clarification') returns null when terminal (:566).

studio_guided_sessions has no terminal timestamp column. expires_at is immutable (V14 identity trigger) and equals createdAt + maxSessionSeconds (default 600 s). V15 capture closes on a terminal/FINALIZING state OR expires_at <= clock_timestamp() (V15:158-159).

studio_publication_immutable() is ONE function bound BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE to bases/observations/preparations/admissions/publications, and BEFORE DELETE to attempts (V15:298-304). FK chain: publication_admissions → publication_preparations → publication_observations. ui_test_revisions and publications reference bases.

Learning-session approvedOrigins come from ObservedReplayPins.policy(scope).allowedOrigins, which is the configured TrustedPolicy (GuidedProductionSessionAccess:67-68). Replay binds currentPolicyHash = hash(configured TrustedPolicy) (ObservedReplayAuthorizer:92,120).

So only the public claim() (:77-80) and the controller route are legacy-only. StudioContractTest:414-415 has record-parity rows for AdmissionRequest/AdmissionResponse. openapi components.schemas.AdmissionRequest (:3669) and AdmissionResponse (:3686) are referenced only by claimAdmission (:1616, :1636). A fixture already exists: ObservedPublicationFixture.admitObserved(observed, admission, executionId, runner, admissionId) (:644-680), used by ProgressCallbackIT:95.

a_closedCodes.principle: Reuse an existing code wherever its meaning fits. Add a code only where none fits, and add it only to the vocabulary that carries that kind of code. No AC-1/4/5/6 code is an execution error_code. The ExecutionErrorCode / openapi ExecutionErrorCode / V13 CHECK set is therefore NOT changed, and V19 MUST NOT name ck_ui_test_executions_error_code (ErrorCodeVocabularyTest would go red, correctly). Guided codes have no DB CHECK, so 'through the vocabulary incl. migration' means the following for guided codes: the v3 schema enum, regenerated bundles (tools/build-studio-observed-schemas.cjs), the Java emitter and the 012B/008 frontend narrative row, all in one C step. No migration is needed, and none is invented.

policyReasonVocabulary.carrier: A closed Java enum (guided/policy/GuidedPolicyReason). It is carried on the validator rejection (a GuidedSessionException subclass or field, B14's choice) and in the AC-10 audit event field `reasonCode`. It never appears in a public schema.
policyReasonVocabulary.terminalMapping: stopRejected: a POLICY_DENIED rejection that CARRIES a GuidedPolicyReason ends the session FAILED with progress.errorCode = 'POLICY_DENIED'. result.errorCode is an open string, so there is no schema change. failTranslation's allowed set gains POLICY_DENIED. A POLICY_DENIED WITHOUT a reason (the existing password-control refusals, GuidedProposalValidator:350-368) keeps today's mapping to INVALID_CONTRACT byte-for-byte. OBS-007 behaviour is therefore unchanged.
policyReasonVocabulary.loginRequired: These rejections go through the existing rejected-proposal path, so annotateLoginFailure (POLICY_DENIED is already in its set, GuidedTranslationService:1124-1133) runs before stopRejected. A grounding rejection on a login page still yields LOGIN_REQUIRED, which is the AC-4 requirement.
policyReasonVocabulary.repair: Not repairable in this wave. That matches the existing rule that POLICY_DENIED is terminal. Trade-off: a grounding false-negative costs a whole session. OBS-009 D-C measures the rate against the ≥90% gate, and making it repairable later is a one-entry change to the repair set.

a_closedCodes.frontendCoupling: 012B/OBS-008 add narratives for POLICY_NOT_APPROVED and for terminal POLICY_DENIED. FE allowlist class-C entries follow C2b (PO ruling 012B).

b_pruneDesign.scope: studio_guided_sessions.progress (key-level) and studio_guided_model_attempts.safe_result (nulled) for EVERY terminal session past the window. In addition, the V15 publication-table copies (admissions, preparations, observations rows, deleted) for terminal sessions with NO studio_guided_publications row (PO X6-b). Published sessions keep their four publication tables byte-unchanged (PO X6-a).
b_pruneDesign.pruner: New backend/src/main/java/com/citi/put/checks/studio/guided/retention/GuidedObservationPruner.java (@Component, @Scheduled fixedDelayString '${studio.guided-authoring.retention.pruner-delay-ms:3600000}'), next to GuidedSessionReaper and with the same thin shape. The core scheduling/partitioning/RetentionPruner is NOT used: it drops partitions, and these tables are not partitioned. The pruner selects up to batch-size candidates (`SELECT session_id FROM studio_guided_sessions WHERE pruned_at IS NULL AND state IN (<terminal>) AND expires_at + ?::interval <= clock_timestamp() ORDER BY expires_at LIMIT ? FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, in its own short transaction), then calls `SELECT studio_guided_prune_session(?, ?::interval)` once per session, each in its own transaction. The function re-checks everything under the row lock. Failure of one session is logged with sessionId + SQLState only and does not stop the batch.
b_pruneDesign.predicate: state ∈ {SUCCEEDED, PUBLICATION_CONFLICT, FAILED, UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, CANCELLED, EXPIRED} AND pruned_at IS NULL AND expires_at + window <= clock_timestamp(). This is judged ONLY in SQL, on the DB clock. Anchor = expires_at, because there is no terminal timestamp. It is immutable and ≥ the last possible capture instant (V15:159), so 'capture closed' holds by construction. A terminal state also closes capture (V15:158). FINALIZING is never terminal and is never pruned. No V19 terminal_at column is added: it would need a write in every stop() path, for at most 600 s of precision.

keyLevelProgressPrune.rule: RETAIN-LIST, not delete-list (fail-closed: any key added later is pruned unless it is listed explicitly).
keyLevelProgressPrune.why: result(), the projector, publicationCommitted and the post-terminal teardown/evidence writers read or write only these keys. `detail` is the closed {stepId, loginStepsPresent} (IDs/booleans). Everything else is pruned, including observation, executionEvidence, clarification, resolvedClarifications, observationRefresh, origin, translationBootstrap(+Evidence), translationAcquisition, modelReservations, secretReleaseDecisions, publicationSnapshotIdentity, documentId, generation, observationHash and evidenceHash.
keyLevelProgressPrune.singleSource: SQL function studio_guided_progress_retained_keys() RETURNS text[] IMMUTABLE in V19. The prune function and the session prune guard both read it. Java holds no copy. If OBS-013 needs a post-terminal progress key, V20 CREATE OR REPLACEs this function in the same D unit (AR-1 puts recording state in a V20 table, so none is expected).

b_pruneDesign.sqlFunction_V19: CREATE FUNCTION studio_guided_prune_session(p_session_id varchar, p_window interval) RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE plpgsql: (1) IF p_window IS NULL OR p_window < interval '1 hour' → RAISE. (2) SELECT the session FOR UPDATE; RETURN false if not found, pruned_at IS NOT NULL, state is not terminal, or expires_at + p_window > clock_timestamp(). (3) UPDATE studio_guided_sessions SET progress = (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(key,value),'{}'::jsonb) FROM jsonb_each(progress) WHERE key = ANY(studio_guided_progress_retained_keys())), pruned_at = clock_timestamp(). (4) UPDATE studio_guided_model_attempts SET safe_result = NULL WHERE session_id = p AND status IN ('APPLIED','REJECTED','SUPERSEDED','UNKNOWN_CALL') AND safe_result IS NOT NULL. Do NOT touch updated_at. (5) IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM studio_guided_publications WHERE session_id = p): DELETE FROM studio_guided_publication_admissions, then _preparations, then _observations WHERE session_id = p (FK order). (6) RETURN true. Bases and attempts are never deleted (see e).
b_pruneDesign.sessionPruneGuard_V19: ALTER TABLE studio_guided_sessions ADD COLUMN pruned_at timestamptz. New BEFORE UPDATE trigger function studio_guided_prune_guard: IF OLD.pruned_at IS NOT NULL: RAISE if NEW.pruned_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.pruned_at ('guided prune is write-once') or if (NEW.progress - studio_guided_progress_retained_keys()) <> '{}' ('pruned progress cannot regain content'). ELSIF NEW.pruned_at IS NOT NULL: RAISE unless OLD.state is terminal AND NEW.state = OLD.state AND (NEW.progress - retained) = '{}'. Partial index ix_guided_session_prune ON studio_guided_sessions(expires_at) WHERE pruned_at IS NULL.

d_attemptGuard_V19.statement: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION studio_guided_translation_attempt_guard(). The trigger binding tr_guided_attempt_guard (V14) stays.
d_attemptGuard_V19.body: IF TG_OP='DELETE' THEN RAISE 'guided attempt is immutable'. Then: IF the parent session (studio_guided_sessions.session_id = OLD.session_id) has pruned_at IS NOT NULL: RETURN NEW only if OLD.status IN ('APPLIED','REJECTED','SUPERSEDED','UNKNOWN_CALL') AND OLD.safe_result IS NOT NULL AND NEW.safe_result IS NULL AND (to_jsonb(NEW) - 'safe_result') = (to_jsonb(OLD) - 'safe_result'). Otherwise RAISE 'guided attempt is pruned' (this also closes any late non-null settlement on a pruned session). If the session is not pruned, run the V14 body VERBATIM (non-terminal transitions unchanged).
d_attemptGuard_V19.permits: ONLY terminal safe_result non-null → NULL, ONLY after the session is pruned, with every other column byte-identical (updated_at included).
negativeTests_GuidedGovernanceMigrationI: For a terminal APPLIED attempt on a PRUNED session, changing each other column alone is refused: session_id, attempt_id, request_id, attempt_number, kind, identity, request_digest, translator_id, lease_until, reservation_key, settlement_key, status, input_tokens, output_tokens, created_at, updated_at (16 cases, one per column, each also with safe_result→NULL in the same UPDATE).
safe_result → a different non-null value is refused. safe_result NULL → non-null is refused.
safe_result → NULL on a terminal attempt of an UNPRUNED session is refused (V14 behaviour).
RESERVED/CALLING attempts on an unpruned session: the existing V14 transitions still pass (positive control). CALLING→RESERVED is still refused.
On a pruned session, a RESERVED/CALLING attempt settling with non-null safe_result is refused.
DELETE is refused for every status.
Positive: the one permitted transition succeeds, and to_jsonb(row) - 'safe_result' is identical before and after.

e_publicationCopies_X6.ruling: PO X6 (b) is SAFE for this wave and is implemented. Mechanism: row DELETE (not content nulling) of studio_guided_publication_admissions → _preparations → _observations for terminal, pruned sessions with no publication row. Nulling would need DROP NOT NULL plus a rewrite of the unnamed closed-shape CHECKs on the V15 tables, which is a larger and more fragile edit than one narrowed trigger.
e_publicationCopies_X6.guard_V19: CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION studio_publication_immutable(). The V15 trigger bindings on all five tables and attempts stay. Body: IF TG_OP='DELETE' AND TG_TABLE_NAME IN ('studio_guided_publication_admissions','studio_guided_publication_preparations','studio_guided_publication_observations') AND EXISTS (session with pruned_at IS NOT NULL AND state terminal) AND NOT EXISTS (studio_guided_publications row for OLD.session_id) THEN RETURN OLD. Otherwise RAISE 'publication evidence immutable'.
e_publicationCopies_X6.whySafe: (1) A terminal state is immutable (V14 identity trigger) and publication requires FINALIZING (V15 attempt guard), so a session pruned without a publication row can never gain one later. (2) Production readers of these rows run only while publishing (GuidedPlanPublisher:204,354,442, verified by @po). Replay verifies by hash (ObservedRevisionVerifier:205). (3) No other table has an FK to these three except admissions → preparations → observations, and the deletion order is FK order.
e_publicationCopies_X6.retained: studio_guided_publication_bases and studio_guided_publication_attempts are retained for every session. They hold identity, hashes, runAuthorization, initialContext {kind, origin}, replayRequirements, validator receipts and failure codes, and no observation nodes, execution evidence or proposals. Deleting bases would also force deleting attempts (FK) and their audit value. This is consistent with X6-b, whose named content is observation, execution_evidence and proposal. AC-2 must disclose the retained base/attempt fields, including initialContext.origin.
negativeTests: UPDATE of any column on any of the five tables is refused, pruned or not.
DELETE on bases, publications and attempts is refused even for a pruned, never-published session.

DELETE on the three tables is refused when (i) the session is non-terminal, (ii) the session is terminal but pruned_at IS NULL, or (iii) a studio_guided_publications row exists (a published session that is pruned).

AC-3 IT: after prune, a published session's rows in all four publication tables are byte-identical (compare to_jsonb row sets) and replay of its revision still verifies. A never-published session's three tables have zero rows and its base row is unchanged.

b_pruneDesign.window: application.yml (B14, SOLE OWNER): studio.guided-authoring.retention.observation-window: ${STUDIO_GUIDED_OBSERVATION_RETENTION:30d}. This equals studio.execution.evidence-retention, so video and observations age out together. Also pruner-delay-ms 3600000 and batch-size 100. Properties validation: window ≥ PT24H, otherwise start-up fails. The DB floor is 1 hour as defence in depth.
it_GuidedObservationPrunerIT: result() and the projector output are byte-identical before and after prune for (i) a FAILED/LOGIN_REQUIRED session and (ii) a SUCCEEDED published session.
Pruned content is gone: progress keys equal the retained subset, and safe_result is NULL on every terminal attempt.
A session inside the window is not pruned. A FINALIZING session is not pruned. A second prune returns false.
Published session: publication rows unchanged and replay still verifies. Never-published session: the three copy tables are empty.
The window is judged on the DB clock: back-date expires_at via SQL (the identity trigger forbids changing it, so seed the session with an old expires_at). Do NOT use a JVM clock.

tables_V19: studio_guided_csi_guards(csi_id varchar(20) PRIMARY KEY). The per-CSI lock row, upserted (INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) and then SELECT … FOR UPDATE inside the start transaction.

studio_guided_csi_token_days(csi_id varchar(20), budget_day date, input_tokens bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(input_tokens>=0), output_tokens bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK(output_tokens>=0), PRIMARY KEY(csi_id,budget_day)). A trigger refuses DELETE and refuses any decrease of either column (monotone).
Expression index ix_guided_session_live_csi ON studio_guided_sessions((document->'scope'->>'csiId')) WHERE state NOT IN (<terminal>).
c_perCsiCounters.concurrency: In GuidedSessionService.start, AFTER the idempotent-replay lookup (an existing key returns without counting) and BEFORE the session insert, in the same transaction: lock the guard row, then count sessions for the CSI WHERE state NOT IN (terminal) AND expires_at > clock_timestamp(). Refuse if count >= max-concurrent-sessions. The count is derived under the lock rather than kept as a counter, so there is no decrement to lose when a session ends.
c_perCsiCounters.dailyTokens: UTC day on the DB clock: budget_day = (clock_timestamp() AT TIME ZONE 'UTC')::date, computed in SQL. At start: require remaining input > 0 AND remaining output > 0 (no charge). At each model reservation (the transaction that inserts the studio_guided_model_attempts row, in GuidedTranslationStore): upsert today's row, then ONE conditional UPDATE … SET input_tokens = input_tokens + :inCeiling, output_tokens = output_tokens + :outCeiling WHERE csi_id=? AND budget_day=<today> AND input_tokens + :inCeiling <= :inLimit AND output_tokens + :outCeiling <= :outLimit. The affected-row count is the verdict (AdmissionCas pattern). The charge is the attempt's identity.inputCeiling/outputCeiling with no refund. Late usage above the ceiling (recordLateUsage) adds the excess unconditionally (it is already spent). This matches studio_guided_model_usage_report's GREATEST(ceiling, actual). A zero-row verdict follows the existing acquisition REFUSED/BUDGET_EXCEEDED path, and the session ends FAILED with BUDGET_EXCEEDED.

defaults.keys: studio.guided-authoring.csi-budget.{max-concurrent-sessions, daily-model-input-tokens, daily-model-output-tokens} with env overrides STUDIO_GUIDED_CSI_MAX_CONCURRENT / _DAILY_INPUT_TOKENS / _DAILY_OUTPUT_TOKENS
defaults.validation: Start-up fails if daily input < maxModelInputTokensTotal, daily output < maxModelOutputTokensTotal, or concurrency < 1. Otherwise a single session could never fit.
defaults.rationale: k = 20 full-ceiling sessions per CSI per day bounds gateway spend per CSI at 20× the worst single session while leaving normal authoring (sessions far below ceiling) unconstrained. It is configurable per deployment. This is an estimate, not a measurement. OBS-009 may tune it from D-C data.

c_perCsiCounters.sessionLimitsUnchanged: GuidedSessionProperties defaults are untouched. The GuidedPlanningIntegrationTest:742 pin stays.
c_perCsiCounters.it_GuidedCsiBudgetIT: Two replicas through SecondApplicationContext against one DB. Limit 1: concurrent starts on one CSI give exactly one 202 and one 429 BUDGET_EXCEEDED. A different CSI is unaffected. Daily budget is seeded to limit − 1: the next reservation is refused and the session ends FAILED/BUDGET_EXCEEDED. Day rollover: seed yesterday's row at the limit, and today's start succeeds. Days are computed by the DB; the test never fakes the JVM clock.

d_budgetExceededResponse.envelope: The v3 guided error envelope, NOT RFC 7807 application/problem+json. No route in this backend emits problem+json. A second error media type on one operation would give clients two parsers for one status. The story's 'problem+json' is read as 'closed machine-readable problem body', which the v3 envelope already is. This is a wording divergence and is recorded here; it is not a scope change.
d_budgetExceededResponse.body: {schemaVersion:3, code:'BUDGET_EXCEEDED', messageCode:'CSI_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS_EXHAUSTED' | 'CSI_DAILY_TOKENS_EXHAUSTED', requestId, retryable:true}. messageCode is an existing free string, so error.schema is unchanged. All pre-existing BUDGET_EXCEEDED refusals keep retryable:false and carry no Retry-After, because per-session ceilings do not reset with time.
d_budgetExceededResponse.retryAfter: Header Retry-After: integer seconds ≥ 1, computed in SQL on the DB clock. Daily = ceil(seconds until the next UTC midnight). Concurrent = ceil(min(expires_at) − clock_timestamp()) over the CSI's live sessions. That is the latest instant a slot is guaranteed to free, so it is an upper bound and not a guess.
d_budgetExceededResponse.where: Only GuidedSessionController's handler (targeted) sets the header, from fields carried on the exception. ChecksExceptionHandler is not touched.
d_budgetExceededResponse.contract_C2b: startGuidedSession gains '429' (Class C, ADR-002 §19/§34.1): oneOf [v3 error (BUDGET_EXCEEDED, per-CSI and the existing per-session source-step bound), PlatformErrorResponse (RATE_LIMITED from RateLimitFilter now that start is EXECUTE)], with header Retry-After {type: integer, minimum: 1}. StudioContractTest status-map row updated. AC-8 classifier: `.*/studio/guided-sessions$` with POST → EXECUTE only (not /cancel or other sub-routes). RateLimitClassifierTest names the positive case and two negatives (GET, POST …/{id}/cancel).

e_auditLogger.logbackEntry: Add a dedicated appender AUDIT_JSON (ConsoleAppender, LoggingEventCompositeJsonEncoder with providers timestamp, loggerName, `arguments`, a constant pattern {"service":"${SERVICE_NAME}","stream":"studio-audit"} and NO mdc provider, so unrelated MDC never leaks into SIEM) and `<logger name="com.citi.put.checks.audit.studio" level="INFO" additivity="false"><appender-ref ref="AUDIT_JSON"/></logger>`. INFO is pinned so that lowering com.citi.put.checks cannot silence the audit. additivity=false prevents double emission through JSON_CONSOLE. SIEM forwarding selects on stream=studio-audit; that is deployment (OBS-009).
e_auditLogger.emitter: One final class guided/audit/StudioActionAudit with one method per event. The message is the constant eventType. All fields are passed as StructuredArguments, so no field is ever interpolated into the message. Emission happens in TransactionSynchronization.afterCommit, so a rolled-back admission is never audited as admitted.

eventShape_closed.origin: the approved-origin string, emitted ONLY after it is verified to be a member of the session's approvedOrigins. Otherwise the literal 'UNAPPROVED'. It is never page-derived text.
eventShape_closed.targetRole: role from the closed ARIA role set, or 'page'/'none'

AR-2.f_sideEffectDefault: Default CLARIFY_FIRST. The governed policy document carries sideEffectStance ∈ {ALLOW, CLARIFY_FIRST, DENY} and destructiveVocabulary (1..64 lowercase phrases, each ≤ 64 chars). On create/version, an omitted stance is materialized server-side as CLARIFY_FIRST, and an omitted vocabulary as the baseline from application.yml studio.guided-authoring.policy.default-destructive-vocabulary: [delete, remove, erase, destroy, purge, pay, transfer, send money, submit order, place order, confirm payment, cancel subscription, close account, deactivate, revoke]. Both are stored IN the document, so the hash and the audit cover them. Bare 'submit' is deliberately excluded (login forms). Matching is case-insensitive whole-word/phrase on the sanitized safe label and on the authored step text, or on the referenced saved-input text. CLARIFY_FIRST raises at most ONE clarification per session, before the first side-effecting dispatch: reason SIDE_EFFECT_CONFIRMATION, promptCode CONFIRM_ACTION, exactly one choice {safeLabel = authored step text (truncated to 256), labelSource AUTHORED, nodeId = proposed target node id, bindingId null}. Declining = the existing cancel or clarification expiry. The confirmation is recorded in progress (a pruned key). The OBS-007 end-to-end regression seeds ALLOW explicitly. A separate test covers the default.
AR-2.g_replayPolicy: Replay keeps its published snapshot. The governed policy applies to LEARNING sessions only. ObservedReplayPins, ObservedReplayAuthorizer, currentPolicyHash and referencePolicyHash are not changed by OBS-014. Approving v2 changes no replay binding or verdict for an existing revision, and an IT asserts this (ObservationPolicyIT: approve v2 → replay of a v1-learned revision binds the same currentPolicyHash and verifies). Residual for PO placement, not fixed here: learning origins/read rules then come from the governed object while replay still reads the configured TrustedPolicy. That is two configuration sources for one application. Unifying them is a follow-up (candidate OBS-009/OBS-015), and it is named in AC-2.

stopConditions: S-1 Any V19 statement that edits V12–V18 files, names ck_ui_test_executions_error_code, or adds an ExecutionErrorCode value → STOP (not ruled here; it would turn ErrorCodeVocabularyTest red by design).

S-2 A post-terminal PRODUCTION read of a pruned progress key, of a terminal attempt's safe_result, or of the three publication copy tables for a never-published session is found (beyond those listed in verifiedFacts) → STOP and report the reader. Do not add keys to the retain list to make a test pass.
S-3 GuidedObservationPrunerIT shows result()/projector output differing before vs after prune → STOP. Never relax the byte-equality.

S-4 GuidedTranslationStore.finishAttempt or recordLateUsage is reachable for a pruned session in production → add a precheck refusing with existing EXPIRED 409 before SQL. If that needs more than a precheck, STOP.
S-5 The runner and backend policy hashes differ on any shared vector → STOP. Canonicalization must be fixed at the contract (C lane), not in one side.

S-6 The side-effect classification (AC-6) needs a page signal that the sanitized observation does not already carry → STOP and escalate to @architect. Adding observation fields exported to the model is out of bounds for OBS-014 (Dev Notes: must not export more page content).

S-7 A re-pointed admission test's observed-path refusal differs from the oracle ruled above → record the actual code. If it is still a refusal with zero writes, update the oracle by name and record it. If the CAS property under test becomes unreachable through claimObserved, DROP it by name with the covering case named. Never keep AdmissionCasService.claim() (or any public legacy entry) for tests.
S-8 Approver-group membership cannot be read from BffAuthenticationToken/UserIdentity → STOP and escalate (the approval route stays fail-closed). Do not invent an identity source.
S-9 Under the default destructive vocabulary, the OBS-007 fixture end-to-end (seeded ALLOW) fails on a destructive-verb refusal → report the label. Do not trim the vocabulary silently.
S-10 Any partial C2b landing (policy routes without runner-context fields or the fixture seeding) → the whole S3 unit is rolled forward together or not at all (RK-2).
tradeOffs: SQL prune function vs Java prune logic: chosen SQL. The predicate, the DB clock, the retain list and the FK-ordered deletes are atomic under one row lock, matching the V14/V15 guard style. Cost: plpgsql is covered only by ITs (no unit tests).
Row delete vs nulling for the publication copies: chosen delete. Nulling needs DROP NOT NULL and a rewrite of unnamed V15 CHECKs. Cost: base and attempt rows survive (disclosed).

Charge the ceiling with no refund: monotone, simple, and consistent with the usage report. Cost: it over-counts real usage, so effective daily capacity is below the token number (mitigated by k = 20).
Count-under-lock for concurrency vs a counter: no lost decrement on crash or expiry. Cost: one indexed count per start.

POLICY_DENIED + internal reason vs three new public codes: one public code and an honest terminal errorCode, while OBS-007 password refusals keep their mapping. Cost: the reason is visible only in audit and the attempt record, not in the result body.

A separate session-policy freeze table vs extending scope/runAuthorization: avoids touching three closed shapes (V14 identity trigger, V15 base CHECK, v3 session schema). Cost: one extra join when the runner context is built.
